message.reasoning_content:
Key bugs: parse_u64 sets out=0 first, violating "out unchanged on failure" (e.g. "12x" leaves out=0, or overflow). Also overflow: out*10 wraps, no UINT64_MAX check — "1844674407378" wraps silently, returns true. Also empty string: returns true with out=0, contract says nonempty required. Also noexcept but overflow check fine.

Registry: get returns string_view into vector while holding lock_guard — view valid after unlock, but add may push_back causing reallocation/remove of strings, invalidating views (dangling). Also get(i) no bounds check. Also readers retaining values while writers add: string_view may dangle after push_back realloc. Fix: return std::string (copy) or use shared_ptr / stable storage (deque of unique_ptr) so views remain valid; or copy under lock.

Also mutex lock_guard in get: fine. But get returns view to element that add may move — dangling. Also no bounds check on i (style/bug minor).

Also parse_u64 noexcept fine.

Minimal triggers:
1. out unchanged on failure: parse_u64("1x", out) with out=5 → out becomes 0 (violates unchanged). Actually out=0 assignment at start; loop sees '1' then 'x' returns false with out=1. So out changed.
2. empty: parse_u64("", out) returns true, contract requires nonempty → violation.
3. overflow: "1844674407378" (UINT64_MAX+1) wraps, returns true, out garbage. Also "99999999999999999999" wraps.
4. Registry dangling: get(0) then add long string causing realloc → view dangles. Also get(i) out of bounds → UB.
5. Also get returns view while lock held — fine, but readers retaining after get returns while add keeps calling: contract violation.

Fixes: parse_u64: check empty, accumulate in temp, only assign out on success, detect overflow via temp > (UINT64_MAX - d)/10. Registry: return std::string copy, or store std::unique_ptr<std::string> in vector so push_back doesn't invalidate pointers... push_back of unique_ptr still invalidates vector references but not the pointed-to strings, so string_view to *ptr stays valid. But get returning string_view to **? get returns names[i] view of string contents — with unique_ptr, view points to heap string, stable. But add replacing? add only appends. So fix: vector<std::unique_ptr<std::string>>; get returns std::string_view(*names[i]) — valid until name removed (never). Also bounds check.

Also get returning std::string copy simplest fix.

Findings:
1. parse_u64 writes out=0 before validation → failure leaves out changed (e.g. out=7, parse "12a" → out=12, false).
2. empty accepted (returns true) — contract requires nonempty.
3. overflow wraps silently, returns true (e.g. "1844674407378" or "99999999999999999999").
4. Registry::get returns string_view into vector; concurrent add push_back may realloc/move strings → retained view dangles (readers retain while writers add).
5. get(i) no bounds check → UB for i≥size.
6. maybe: get returns view while holding lock_guard — fine. Or noexcept on parse fine. Maybe note: mutex doesn't protect retained view lifetime — same as 4. Could mention fix options.

Fix parse: 
bool parse_u64(std::string_view s, std::uint64_t& out) noexcept {
    std::uint64_t v = 0;
    if (s.empty()) return false;
    for (char c : s) {
        if (c < '0' || c > '9') return false;
        std::uint64_t d = c - '0';
        if (v > (UINT64_MAX - d) / 10) return false; // careful: (max-d)/10
        v = v * 10 + d;
    }
    out = v;
    return true;
}
Note leading zeros allowed: "0000000000000000000184467440737" — leading zeros with 20+ digits: overflow check triggers on zeros? v stays 0 for zeros, then overflow check at last digits fine. But "00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000" (many zeros) → v=0, fine, accepted. Good. But "0" * 30 then value: fine.

Edge: overflow check with v > (max-d)/10: for v==max/10 and d... standard check: if (v > (UINT64_MAX - d)/10) return false. Correct.

Registry fix: return std::string (copy under lock) — simplest; or store unique_ptr<std::string> so views stay valid; add bounds check.
